text:
alex_k: hey folks — pulled an NSYS trace from a repro of the latency regression on the kvcache-prefetch path. timeline looks like memcpy bursts on stream 3 interleaving with small kernels on stream 0, and the copy engine seems saturated. curious if this is a kernel-selection/batcher interaction or just host-memory behavior. attaching quick screenshot link: https://imgur.com/example (full rep stored in s3)

maria_r: can you paste the nsys CLI you used? any cpuctxsw/OS trace enabled? also which CUDA driver + model build?

alex_k: ran: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn,nvtx --output=trace.kvcache` on prod-like VM. driver 520.61, runtime built from main @ 9f3a2c8 (the batching heuristic change landed there). no --cpuctxsw. sample trace shows repeated pattern: hostToDevice memcpy (1.2–3.5ms) -> 30–80ms idle on CPU -> kernel launch `multi_head_attn_fwd` that blocks until memcpy done. feels like host memcpy serialization + CPU scheduling gap.

tj: two quick hypotheses: 1) pageable->device copies are serializing the copy engine because they fall back to staged copies; 2) our batcher now coalesces many small KV prefetches into big memcpy which increases copy size and monopolizes the copy engine. both could cause other streams' kernels to stall if copy engine is saturated or if there are implicit synchronizations. try pinned host allocations or `cuMemHostAlloc` path.

sam_w: I also noticed in a separate perf run that the worker thread doing prefetch gets preempted by GC for ~40ms in some traces — that creates the 30–80ms window. did we change any python threading or GC heuristics in the recent commit? @maria_r might know about the batcher change.

maria_r: yes the batcher change from PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4587 (commit 9f3a2c8) increases max_coalesce_bytes for kvcache prefetch to reduce RPC overhead. unintended side-effect: larger memcpy sizes. we tuned it to reduce RPC but didn't re-run with pinned allocation. good catch.

perf-bot: quick automated analysis: found 12 memcpy peaks > 2ms on stream 3, copy engine utilization ~86% during peak window, and CPU context-switch spikes aligning with delayed kernel submissions. Suggest re-run with `--cpuctxsw` and `--trace=osrt,cuda,nvtx` to capture OS-level scheduling. Also try `--sample=none` to avoid sampling noise.

alex_k: thanks. proposed repro steps for next run:
```
# capture with OS scheduling
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --cpuctxsw --output=trace.kvcache.osrt
# enable additional envs
export TF_CUDA_HOST_ALLOC=pinned
# or use our patched allocator
export RW_USE_PINNED_PREFETCH=1
```

maria_r: also add NVTX ranges around the batcher and kvcache prefetch so we can correlate: `nvtxRangePushA("batcher:coalesce")`/`nvtxRangePop()` in the hot path. that makes deconvolution of overlapping streams much easier in the UI.

tj: another quick debug: try forcing smaller coalesce size (e.g., 64KB) to see if latency improves. if smaller copies fix it, then it's copy-engine saturation + CPU preemption amplification.

sam_w: I'll grep the trace for `OS_RUNTIME: sched_switch` and post a short snippet. if worker gets scheduled out, we'll see prefetch started but memcpy completion delayed.

alex_k: action items: (1) sam rerun with pinned host allocation + nvtx ranges + cpuctxsw (2) sam/tj test smaller coalesce size locally (3) if repro holds, revert commit 9f3a2c8's coalesce increase and run perf A/B. I'll upload new traces to s3 and ping this thread. :thumbsup:

maria_r: sounds good — also flagging this for 2h postmortem next week if we confirm regression. cc @eng-oncall
